binaries.name: journalctl
binaries.why: Read a systemd journal from a file or directory with --file or --directory (journal_export), and check its structure with --verify. The journal is a binary format that journalctl reads; this pack's dissect.target route (linux_triage) reads it as well, and the two have not been compared here.

install.brew: not available on macOS; analyse on a Linux host

binaries.name: debsums
binaries.why: Compare packaged files on a Debian-family host with the hashes the acquired package database records. That is triage against the examined machine's own database, not an independent trust anchor (packages/integrity).

binaries.name: rpm
binaries.why: Verify packaged files against an acquired RPM database on a Red Hat-family host with -V, reporting which attribute differs. Run it with --noscripts --nodeps so that no verification script from the evidence runs; the examiner confirms on the installed version, against a trial database, that those options are honoured for -V before relying on them (packages/integrity).
binaries.licence: GPL-2.0-or-later AND LGPL-2.0-or-later (as Homebrew's formula metadata gives it)

binaries.name: ausearch
binaries.why: Read the kernel audit log, where the estate had auditd on: execve with arguments, and file access by rule. No skill of this pack names it yet; the skill that will (logs/auditd) is planned for a later change.

binaries.name: debugfs
binaries.why: Read ext2/3/4 internals: an inode's fields, creation time included where the inode holds it, extent trees and the journal (logdump). It opens a volume read-only unless given -w, which evidence never gets.
binaries.licence: GPL-2.0-or-later AND LGPL-2.0-or-later AND LGPL-2.0-only AND BSD-3-Clause AND MIT (e2fsprogs, as Homebrew's formula metadata gives it)

binaries.name: xfs_db
binaries.why: Inspect XFS superblocks, allocation groups, inodes and free-space metadata in read-only mode (-r).

binaries.name: btrfs
binaries.why: Read Btrfs superblocks, trees, subvolumes and device membership without mounting the evidence.

binaries.name: lvs
binaries.why: Enumerate Linux LVM physical volumes, volume groups and logical volumes (lvs, with pvs and vgs from the same package) when a disk's partition table only exposes an LVM container. Prefer the dissect.target route (linux_triage), which does not activate anything.
